chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, from whoever mentioned it, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalanisi, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: Indeed I saw in a dream that I said to you: Fighting alongside other than the Imam whose obedience is obligatory is forbidden, like carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine. And you said to me: It is like that.
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is like that, it is like that.

key_terms.الدَّم: blood — forbidden for consumption in Islamic law
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ الْمَفْرُوضِ طَاعَتُهُ: the Imam whose obedience is obligatory — a technical Shia term referring to the divinely-appointed Imam from the household of the Prophet
key_terms.الْمَنَام: the dream — considered in Islamic tradition as a significant form of spiritual communication
key_terms.الْمَيْتَة: carrion — flesh of an animal that died without proper Islamic slaughter, forbidden by the Quran
key_terms.لَحْم الْخِنْزِير: flesh of swine — categorically forbidden in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about fighting under a leader other than the rightful Imam?
ai.summary: In this hadith, the narrator Bashir al-Dahhan relates to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) a prophetic dream he experienced, in which he informed the Imam that fighting under any leader other than the divinely-appointed Imam is as forbidden as consuming carrion, blood, or pork — three categorically prohibited substances in the Quran (2:173). When the narrator recounts that in his dream the Imam confirmed this ruling, the actual Imam emphatically repeats the confirmation twice: 'It is like that, it is like that.' This narration firmly establishes the Shia doctrinal position that armed jihad is only legitimate under the command of the rightful, divinely-designated Imam, and participation in any other armed conflict is categorically haram.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Al Tatary, from the one who mentioned it, from Ali Bin Al No’man, from Suweyd Al Qalanasy, from Bashir Al Dahhan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I saw in the dream that I said to you<sup>asws</sup> that the fighting alongside other than the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, the obedience to whom is Obligatoty, is Prohibited like the (consumption of) the dead, and the blood, and flesh of the swine, so you<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘It is like that’.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is like that, it is like that’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Tatriy has narrated from those who he has mentioned in his book - from Ali ibn af-Nu’man from Suwayd af-Qalanisiy from Bashir al-Dahhan who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I saw a dream in which I said to you, “Fighting alongside one who is not an Imam, obedience to whom is obligatory, is unlawful just like consuming dead animals, blood and pork for food. You said to me (in my dream), “That is how it is.’”
Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘That is how it is. That is how it is.’”
